customManagers.description: Testcontainers images are plain string literals in TypeScript, so no built-in manager reads them. The file list is explicit: a new file that boots a container has to be added here.
The manually invoked Alertmanager live test pins its three images as module constants.
BuildKit is a pipeline variable rather than an image key, so the gitlabci manager does not see it.
The manually invoked Argo CD live test pins its kind node image as a shell variable, and no built-in manager reads shell scripts.

packageRules.description: Bun is pinned in five places across four files and four managers. Split updates would leave the container image on one Bun and the pipeline runtime on another, so they move as one branch.
drizzle-kit generates against the ORM schema surface, so drizzle-orm and drizzle-kit have to move at the same version. ioredis rides along as the shared Valkey client.
The coverage provider is version-locked to the runner it instruments.

Client and server are published from one source tree and are only tested against each other at the same version. The sdk package is deliberately excluded: it sits on its own version line, so grouping it here would block both.
The Argo CD live test runs a hand-pinned ARGOCD_VERSION that no manager reads, and Argo CD 3.4 is tested only up to Kubernetes 1.35. Move this cap together with ARGOCD_VERSION.

Every non-major update across all managers lands in one weekly branch. It sits after the named groups so it overrides them for non-major updates, which still move together inside this branch; the named groups keep coupled packages together for majors. Majors stay one branch per group because each can need a code or runtime migration, and one broken major would otherwise block every other update.

A replacement swaps one package name for a different one, so it changes dependency identity rather than version, and the npm cooldown preset deliberately exempts it. Hold it behind the dashboard so review does not read it as a routine bump.

Last on purpose. packageRules apply top to bottom, so this overrides the fix type that config:recommended sets for runtime dependencies. release-please reads fix as a patch release and would publish an image for every dependency bump.
